proposed_comments.title: Register status callback before starting receiver
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] Register the status callback before starting the pipe receiver
**Severity:** `medium`

`StatusWindow` constructs `StatusPage`, whose `MainViewModel` assigns `IPCMessageReceivedCallback`. Starting the receiver first leaves a window in which an arriving status message fails the callback-null check and is discarded without being queued. Construct the window before starting reception; activation can remain last. Later updates may recover the display, so this fixes the registration gap rather than guaranteeing delivery of every startup message.

```suggestion
            _mainWindow = new StatusWindow();
            _ipcManager.Start();
```

confidence.rationale: Exact caller chain assigns the callback only after Start; the receiving delegate drops rather than enqueues when callback is null. Source-order proof only, no claim of runtime timing reproduction.

proposed_comments.title: Harvest Workspaces assets at the WinUI installation path
proposed_comments.body:
### [P2] Harvest the launcher assets at their new WinUI installation path
**Severity:** `medium`

#### Affected paths
`WorkspacesLauncherUI.WinUI.csproj` copies the icons to `WinUI3Apps/Assets/Workspaces`. The matching installer work belongs in `installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/Workspaces.wxs` and `generateAllFileComponents.ps1`.

#### Current behavior and impact
The generic WinUI harvest enumerates only top-level files. The existing Workspaces harvest instead targets the old root `Assets/Workspaces` directory. Neither includes the new app-local directory. `StatusWindow.xaml` refers to `/Assets/Workspaces/Workspaces.ico`, and `IconHelper` resolves its fallback from `AppContext.BaseDirectory/Assets/Workspaces/DefaultIcon.ico`; the old root copy does not satisfy these paths. Both icons are present in the Release build output but absent from the current generated WinUI component list. This establishes a missing installation payload, not a claim that the launcher necessarily crashes.

#### Required change
Keep the old asset component for the Workspaces Editor. Add a separate WinUI asset directory and file list, generate its file component into the existing `WorkspacesComponentGroup`, and add uninstall cleanup for the new directory. `Product.wxs` already references that group, and the installer project already compiles `Workspaces.wxs`.

#### Implementation
Add these definitions beside the existing Workspaces definitions:
```xml
<?define WorkspacesWinUIImagesComponentFiles=?>
<?define WorkspacesWinUIImagesComponentFilesPath=$(var.BinDir)WinUI3Apps\Assets\Workspaces\?>
```
Inside the existing fragment, add:
```xml
<DirectoryRef Id="WinUI3AppsAssetsFolder">
  <Directory Id="WorkspacesWinUIAssetsInstallFolder" Name="Workspaces" />
</DirectoryRef>
<DirectoryRef Id="WorkspacesWinUIAssetsInstallFolder" FileSource="$(var.WorkspacesWinUIImagesComponentFilesPath)">
  <!--WorkspacesWinUIImagesComponentFiles_Component_Def-->
</DirectoryRef>
```
Inside `WorkspacesComponentGroup`, add:
```xml
<Component Id="RemoveWorkspacesWinUIAssetsFolder" Guid="A588FB5C-DFC5-441C-A192-8F427276F288" Directory="WorkspacesWinUIAssetsInstallFolder">
  <RegistryKey Root="$(var.RegistryScope)" Key="Software\Classes\powertoys\components">
    <RegistryValue Type="string" Name="RemoveWorkspacesWinUIAssetsFolder" Value="" KeyPath="yes" />
  </RegistryKey>
  <RemoveFolder Id="RemoveFolderWorkspacesWinUIAssetsFolder" Directory="WorkspacesWinUIAssetsInstallFolder" On="uninstall" />
</Component>
```
Immediately after the existing two Workspaces generator calls, add:
```powershell
Generate-FileList -fileDepsJson "" -fileListName WorkspacesWinUIImagesComponentFiles -wxsFilePath $PSScriptRoot\Workspaces.wxs -depsPath "$PSScriptRoot..\..\..\$platform\Release\WinUI3Apps\Assets\Workspaces\"
Generate-FileComponents -fileListName "WorkspacesWinUIImagesComponentFiles" -wxsFilePath $PSScriptRoot\Workspaces.wxs
```
The generator supplies the new component reference to the existing group, so no new Product group reference is needed. Apply both installer-file changes together.

#### Focused verification
Build with `tools\build\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Release -Path src\modules\Workspaces\WorkspacesLauncherUI.WinUI /restore /t:Rebuild /p:AppxPackageSigningEnabled=false /p:EnableMsixTooling=false`. On a non-UTF-8 compiler default code page, set `$env:CL = '/utf-8'` for that invocation; this selects the source charset without changing the system locale. Confirm both icons under `x64\Release\WinUI3Apps\Assets\Workspaces`; run the exact harvest functions on that output and verify both new File entries, their DirectoryRef, and the generated ComponentRef. The generated Workspaces fragment compiled successfully as a WiX 5.0.2 bound library containing the real icon payloads. Complete MSI linkage, installation/uninstallation, and rendered UI were not exercised.

confidence.rationale: Actual Release icons exist; exact generic generator excludes the nested directory; existing dedicated harvest targets root assets. Remedied actual generated fragment compiles as a bound WiX library. No MSI/UI runtime claim.

summary: Two grounded current-head comments: one apply-ready startup callback-registration reorder and one implementation-ready installer asset-harvest remedy. Exact unmodified upstream and public-literal Launcher UI Release sources compiled; actual bound WiX libraries show zero baseline icons versus both real candidate icon payloads. Forty-three old fork-path deltas were audited rather than copied. Three historical requests consumed, including final Lite/startup-timeout; no cloud-clean, MSI install or UI timing claim. Older 123/135 test-count reports are not reused without their actual execution proof.
